title: A proper morphism is finite near every finite fibre
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $s\in S$. If $f$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and the underlying set $f^{-1}(\{s\})$ is finite, then there is an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq S$ of $s$ such that the restriction $f^{-1}(U)\to U$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. No Noetherian hypothesis on $S$ is imposed.

proof.text: Because f is proper, it is of finite type (and locally of finite type) and universally closed by [pqf-lem-proper-basic]. Applying [pqf-lem-locqf-fibre-discrete] to the finite set f^{-1}(\{s\}) shows that f is quasi-finite at every point of that fibre.

source.place: Tag 02UP proof, first sentence; Morphisms Tags 02NH and 01TI

proof.text: Let U\subseteq X be the open locus where f is quasi-finite, supplied by [lem-sc-quasi-finite-points-open]. By Step 1 every point of f^{-1}(\{s\}) lies in U. Therefore, for Z=X\setminus U, one has s\notin f(Z).

The image f(Z) is closed because f is universally closed by [pqf-lem-proper-basic]. Hence V=S\setminus f(Z) is an open neighbourhood of s. For the inverse-image open W=f^{-1}(V), every point lies in U, so W\subseteq U.

source.place: Tag 02UP proof, sentences concerning Z, f(Z), and the choice of V

proof.text: The restriction f^{-1}(V)\to V is proper by [lem-pc-proper-base-change], since it is the base change of f along the open immersion V\hookrightarrow S. It is locally quasi-finite by [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-restriction-to-opens], applied to the locally quasi-finite morphism U\to S from Step 2 and the open subscheme W=f^{-1}(V)\subseteq U. Therefore [pqf-lem-proper-lqf-finite] makes f^{-1}(V)\to V finite. This is the required neighbourhood.
